claim.summary: Landau's lemma for integrals: L_1 >= 0, g >= 0 continuous on [L_1, infinity) with G(s) = int_{L_1}^infty g(L) e^{-sL} dL convergent for Re s > sigma_1; if a function holomorphic on an open set containing the real half-line (sigma_0, infinity) agrees with G where Re s > sigma_1, then the integral converges for every Re s > sigma_0.
claim.assessment: Working proof of a classical statement, written out: the Taylor series of the continuation at a real point to the right of the abscissa has nonnegative terms when evaluated to the left, and Tonelli's theorem sums it to the integral.

claim.summary: Fejer kernel K_L(w) = 2(1 - cos Lw)/(L w^2); a conjugation-closed multiset of points z with |Im z| <= Delta and sum m_z/(1 + (Re z)^2) finite, infinite allowed (real points and off-line pairs gamma_j +- i delta_j); D_L(tau) = sum m_z K_L(tau - z). (a) The sum converges absolutely, and if all delta_j <= theta then L D_L(tau) >= -4 S_off e^{theta L} for every real tau and L > 0, S_off = sum over the points z of the pairs of m_z/|tau - z|^2. (b) Let tau be real, not a real point, and d the largest distance of a pair at height tau (0 if none). If L D_L(tau) >= -C L^A e^{theta L} for all L >= L_1, with theta >= 0, then every delta_j <= max(theta, d). In particular for tau at no pair's height the bound for all large L holds with exponent theta if and only if no pair is farther than theta from the line; no hypothesis on distinct heights or on the supremum of the distances being attained. For the zeros of zeta (z = (rho - 1/2)/i, Delta = 1/2, the count N(T+1) - N(T) << log T) the one-sided bound with theta = 0 at one such tau is the Riemann hypothesis restated.
claim.assessment: Working proof: the Laplace transform in L of L K_L(w) is 2/(s(s^2 + w^2)); the transform of L D_L is a meromorphic function whose poles off the imaginary axis are at +-delta_j +- i(tau - gamma_j) with residues that cannot cancel, and Landau's lemma moves the abscissa of convergence to theta. The application to zeta uses the classical count of zeros in unit intervals, not read in a source in this cycle.

claim.summary: Finite configuration, Fejer kernel K_L, off-line pairs gamma_j +- i delta_j of multiplicity m_j: (a) D_off(tau) >= - sum m_j e^{delta_j L} min(2L, 8/(L((tau - gamma_j)^2 + delta_j^2))), so if all delta_j <= theta and theta L >= 2 the density is at least -8 M e^{theta L}/(L theta^2); (b) with delta* the largest distance and tau off the heights and midpoints of the pairs at delta*, for every L_1 some L > L_1 has D_L(tau) <= -q' e^{delta* L}/L, q' < q = sum |c_j|^2/(2 sum |c_j|), c_j = m_j/(tau - gamma_j - i delta*)^2; hence D_L(tau) >= -C e^{theta L} for all large L forces delta* <= theta.
claim.assessment: Working proof: two elementary bounds for the kernel at complex arguments; the leading term at the largest distance is a real trigonometric polynomial in L with mean zero, whose negative part has mean at least q.

claim.summary: Fejer kernel K_L(w) = 2(1 - cos Lw)/(L w^2), off-line pairs gamma_j -+ i delta with multiplicities m_j, b = delta L: the off-line part of the density sum_z m_z K_L(tau - z) equals -(2 e^b/L) Re G(tau) + E(tau) with G(tau) = sum m_j e^{-iL(tau - gamma_j)}/(tau - gamma_j + i delta)^2, |E| <= 6 Y/L, Y = sum m_j/((tau - gamma_j)^2 + delta^2); G(tau) = -int_0^inf x e^{-delta x} P(x - L) e^{i(x-L) tau} dx with P(y) = sum m_j e^{-iy gamma_j}; and the real points contribute at most (7/3) L N(2 pi/L), N a local count.

claim.summary: For a nonempty finite multiset R with Phi(s) = sum m_rho/(s - rho): all Re rho <= sigma_0 iff Re Phi > 0 on Re s > sigma_0. For real points Gamma and one conjugate pair gamma +- i delta of multiplicity m, the Laguerre expression L(x) = sum m_w/(x - w)^2 on the real line is negative at x = gamma iff sum over Gamma of m'/(gamma - gamma')^2 < 2m/delta^2, the pair's term is at least -2m/delta^2 and negative only for |x - gamma| < delta, and L >= 0 everywhere when the real points have gaps at most 2 delta/sqrt(m) covering (gamma - delta, gamma + delta).
claim.assessment: Working elementary proofs. The half-plane sign criterion is equivalent to the zero-free statement at every boundary, so it is not a weaker premise; the local real-line (Laguerre, phase-monotonicity) condition cannot fail for an off-line pair farther from the line than half the gap of the real points around it times sqrt(m), while the global count of real zeros detects every pair and is the goal's statement. Finite configurations only; part (a) is the finite model of a known equivalence and no novelty is claimed; the general Hermite-Biehler and de Branges sources are not read.
